headline: Govt approves ninth pay scale for public servants
summary: The new structure will be effective from July 1, with basic salaries for Grade 1 reaching up to 156,000 BDT.
details: The government has approved the proposed ninth pay scale for public servants. The decision was made during a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat on Monday.

The new pay scale will be effective from July 1 of this year. Under this structure, the maximum basic salary for Grade 1 has been set at 156,000 BDT, while the minimum basic salary for Grade 20 has been set at 20,000 BDT.
According to Finance Ministry sources, the implementation of the basic salary increase may be phased. A proposal suggests that 30% of the new basic salary be effective from July 1.
The proposal further suggests that an additional 35% be implemented at the start of next year, with the remaining portion effective from July of the following fiscal year.
Additionally, there are recommendations that various allowances may be implemented starting from January of that same fiscal year.
caption:
Public servants are getting a raise! The government has officially approved the ninth pay scale.

The government has approved the proposed ninth pay scale for public servants. The decision was made during a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat on Monday.

The new pay scale will be effective from July 1 of this year. Under this structure, the maximum basic salary for Grade 1 has been set at 156,000 BDT, while the minimum basic salary for Grade 20 has been set at 20,000 BDT.

According to Finance Ministry sources, the implementation of the basic salary increase may be phased. A proposal suggests that 30% of the new basic salary be effective from July 1.

The proposal further suggests that an additional 35% be implemented at the start of next year, with the remaining portion effective from July of the following fiscal year.

Additionally, there are recommendations that various allowances may be implemented starting from January of that same fiscal year.

headline: 1,163 new cases: Four more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 97, with over 35,000 people infected so far, according to the Directorate General of Health Services.
details: Four people died of dengue in the last 24 hours across Bangladesh, while 1,163 new patients were admitted to hospitals.

According to a press release from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Monday, the new cases were reported across various divisions, including 283 in Khulna and 182 in Dhaka North City Corporation.
Other significant case numbers include 159 in Dhaka division (outside city corporations), 123 in Dhaka South City Corporation, 132 in Barishal, and 120 in Chittagong.
The DGHS reported that a total of 35,846 people have been infected with dengue this year, with 61.9% being men and 38.1% being women.
Out of the total infected, 33,205 patients have recovered and been discharged from hospitals.
The total number of dengue-related deaths in the country has now risen to 97 for the current year.
